article.title: Demostrativos anafóricos en mandarín: alcance de la evidencia experimental
article.part: Información y discurso avanzado — 信息與進階篇章
article.chapter: Tema, foco, elipsis y cadenas referenciales — 主題、焦點、省略與指稱鏈

claims.summary: A Chinese demonstrative may be used anaphorically to refer to an antecedent already established in discourse; Teng distinguishes this from situational deixis.
In the reported Mandarin acceptability experiment, demonstratives were rated significantly higher than definite bare nouns in anaphoric contexts; bare nouns remained possible but less preferred.

claims.sectionKey: Alcance para el mandarín de Taiwán
claims.summary: The experiment recruited participants whose first and primary language was Mandarin through Prolific across available countries and did not report a Taiwan-specific subsample; its findings alone do not establish Taiwan-specific 這/那 rules.

locator.section: Section I, ‘Deictic and anaphoric’, pp. 5–6; examples (1)–(3); Persée lines 43–63

links.notes: Defines anaphora by reference to an established antecedent, contrasts the visible-object deictic example with an anaphoric demonstrative, and states the distinction is independent of new/given information.

Reports the acceptability design, sample and result: demonstratives rated significantly higher; bare nouns remain partly felicitous, with improved ratings in same-situation cases but below demonstratives.

locator.section: § 4.2, p. 224; PDF lines 707–715; experimental stimuli (15)–(16), pp. 224–225

links.notes: Participants were first- and primary-language Mandarin speakers recruited across Prolific-available countries; six were removed. The presented stimulus uses na ge and the paper reports no Taiwan-specific sample or analysis.
